title: Toward Latent Language Model Skills Steering and Optimization: An Empirical Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.29459v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Skills, as a useful abstraction for the procedural capabilities of large language models (LLMs), capture how models perform structured, multi-step reasoning and program execution. Existing approaches typically treat skills as explicit, surface-level constructs specified through prompts or programs, leaving open the question of how such procedural capabilities are represented inside the model and whether they can be manipulated as structured objects in latent space. In this empirical study, we investigate whether procedural LLM skills can be represented as directions in activation space and whether vector-space operations over these directions can express skill-level behaviors. We find that procedural skills admit a vector-space representation: individual skill directions can be activated to shift model behavior; independently extracted directions can compose to form higher-level skills. translated_title: 朝向大语言模型潜在技能的引导与优化：一项实证研究
translated_abstract: 技能作为大语言模型（LLM）程序性能力的一种有用抽象，刻画了模型如何执行结构化的多步推理和程序执行。现有方法通常将技能视为通过提示或程序指定的显式的、表层的构造，这留下了一个悬而未决的问题：这些程序性能力在模型内部是如何被表示的，以及它们能否作为结构化对象在潜在空间中被操纵。在这项实证研究中，我们探究了程序性LLM技能是否可以表示为激活空间中的方向，以及对这些方向进行向量空间运算是否能够表达技能级别的行为。我们发现，程序性技能可以被向量空间表示所刻画：激活单个技能方向可以改变模型行为；独立提取的方向可以组合形成更高层次的技能；对比方向能够产生情境条件化的技能表现。
tldr: 该实证研究首次证明大语言模型的程序性技能可以在激活空间中表示为可操纵的方向，通过对这些方向进行向量空间运算（激活与组合），即可在潜在空间中引导和优化模型的技能级行为。
en_tdlr: This empirical study shows that procedural LLM skills can be represented as directions in activation space, and vector-space operations over these directions enable steering and composing skill-level behaviors in latent space.
